## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin woman of spare and gaunt figure, defined by sharp angles and an absence of curves. Her dark hair, which shows gray streaks that have grown grayer over time, is styled twisted up behind in a hard little knot fastened aggressively with two wire hairpins. She has a lined face with faded, sallow cheeks, hard work-worn hands, and often looks tired, old, and worn.

## Personality

A self-contained and sensible woman of rigid conscience, Marilla Cuthbert possesses a sober demeanour and a stern devotion to duty. She is fundamentally undemonstrative and repressed, viewing displays of deep emotion as unseemly and scorning any betrayals of emotional weakness. In her interactions with children, she is practical and fond of moral lessons, often striving to drill tranquil uniformity of disposition into them while admonishing poor table manners. Despite her proud and uncompromising nature, she harbors deep care, though her uncomfortable ignorance can make her curt or sarcastic, particularly following any self-betrayal. Professionally and practical in her talents, she makes braided mats and is celebrated for her homemade currant wine. Driven by a desire for those in her charge to be fitted to earn their own living, she quietly nurtures personal hopes for their future matches.

## History

Marilla Cuthbert lived at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) for sixty years, carrying the memory of being twitted for her dark looks as a child and a past quarrel with John Blythe whom she refused to forgive [F1, F2, F3]. Her quiet routine changed when she and her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) set out to adopt a [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia) orphan boy, only for a girl named [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to arrive instead [S1, S3]. Though Marilla initially insisted on sending [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) back, she pitied the girl's past and agreed to keep and raise her [S3, S5, S6]. Marilla spent the following years disciplining [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), teaching her prayers, and managing her imaginative mishaps, such as a green hair dyeing incident, an accidentally spiked cake, and a mistaken accusation over an amethyst brooch [S7, S8, S14, S26, S33]. Over time, Marilla developed deep affection for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), realizing how much she cared for her after an ankle injury and ultimately grieving the end of the girl's childhood as she grew [S10, S28, S39]. When [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) suddenly died, Marilla was spared from selling [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) because [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) gave up her college scholarship to stay home and care for Marilla's failing eyesight [S44, S45]. Later, Marilla opened her home to her deceased relative's twin children, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md) Keith, taking them in permanently despite Davy's unruly behavior [S53, S54, S69]. Following [Thomas](../character/thomas-lynde.md) Lynde's death, Marilla arranged for [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) to move into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) so [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) could finally attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) [S74]. In the subsequent years, Marilla remained at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) with [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md) and the twins, regularly welcoming [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) back during college holidays and summer breaks [S79, S81, S82, S85].

## Quotes

> "I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P29](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0029)

> "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P25](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0025)

> “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind P35](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0035)

> "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002)

> "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P4](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0004)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla acts as a mentor and guardian to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), taking her in at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) despite initial shock that she was not a boy. Although Marilla initially intended to send her back, she decides to keep and raise [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) properly, guiding her on religious instruction, bedroom neatness, and proper decorum. Over time, their dynamic evolves into a deep mutual affection, with Marilla offering comfort and guidance while navigating Anne's theatrical emotional outbursts and vivid imagination.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P8](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0008), [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P39](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0039), +23 more_

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Marilla and Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) are neighboring friends who frequently visit each other for tea and news. While [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md) readily voices strong unsolicited opinions on farm matters, politics, and Marilla's domestic decisions, Marilla often relies on her for advice regarding childcare and community affairs. Their close bond allows them to candidly discuss household troubles, attend events together, and manage neighborhood disruptions.

### [Davy Keith](../character/davy-keith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/davy-keith--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla serves as [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) Keith's guardian, exercising authority over him by giving orders and enforcing discipline. Davy's mischievous conduct—ranging from skipping prayers and hiding a toad in Marilla's bed to hiding his sister [Dora](../character/dora.md) and lying—frequently tests Marilla's patience. Despite having to penalize his misbehavior, Marilla maintains a genuine fondness for the boy and laughs over his antics in private.

_Sources: [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P11](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0011), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P36](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0036), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P49](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0049), +15 more_
